title: SGB Redemption: ₹1 Lakh Becomes ₹3.09 Lakh for Early Investors

faq.q: What is a Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB)?
faq.a: SGBs are government securities denominated in grams of gold. They are issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the Government of India and serve as a substitute for holding physical gold.

faq.q: How is the SGB issue price determined?
faq.a: The issue price of SGBs is based on the simple average of the closing price of 999 purity gold, published by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA) Limited, for the last three business days of the week preceding the subscription period.

faq.q: Is the interest earned on SGBs taxable?
faq.a: Yes, the interest of 2.50% per annum paid semi-annually on SGBs is taxable. It is added to your total income and taxed as per your applicable income tax slab rate.

faq.q: Are capital gains from SGBs taxable?
faq.a: For individual investors, capital gains arising from the redemption of SGBs at maturity (after 8 years) are exempt from tax. However, if sold on an exchange before maturity, capital gains may be taxable depending on the holding period.

faq.q: What is the tenure of an SGB?
faq.a: SGBs have a fixed tenure of eight years. However, investors have an exit option available after the fifth year, which can be exercised on interest payment dates.
Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are generally not eligible to invest in SGBs. Only resident individuals, Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs), trusts, universities, and charitable institutions can invest.
